This source tree contains a "Third-Party Modified Version of the Fraunhofer
FDK AAC Codec Library for Android."

The last modification is from Aug 21 2025.

This fdk-aac fork is stripped from parts with patent concerns (i.e. HE
(High Efficiency) and HEv2 profiles). The Fedora Legal team has approved this
fork. https://bugzilla.redhat.com/1501522

general perceptual audio codecs. AAC-ELD is considered the best-performing
full-bandwidth communications codec by independent studies and is widely
deployed. AAC has been standardized by ISO and IEC as part of the MPEG
specifications.

components.name: boost
components.via: 3rdparty/vcpkg.json — asio, beast, json, url, thread, filesystem, …
components.notes: All boost-* vcpkg ports are collapsed into this entry; they share one licence.

components.name: fdk-aac
components.notes: REVIEW: the Fraunhofer FDK AAC licence is not an OSI/FSF-free licence and the FSF considers it GPL-incompatible, so linking it into an AGPL-3.0 binary is a conflict that needs a decision. vcpkg ships the Fedora-approved fork with the patent-encumbered HE/HEv2 profiles stripped. iOS is excluded by an explicit `if(NOT IOS)` guard and Android by the absence of fdk-aac from the *-android vcpkg trees, so this affects desktop only.

components.name: ffmpeg
components.via: present in the vcpkg store only
components.notes: NOT SHIPPED. The ffmpeg services are gated on AVCPP_FOUND (hkp-rt/lib/CMakeLists.txt:32) and 3rdparty/avcpp no longer exists, so nothing defines it and no FFmpeg code is linked. Listed so the store's presence is not mistaken for a shipped dependency. Re-check this entry if avcpp comes back.

components.name: openssl
components.via: 3rdparty/vcpkg.json — TLS for the HTTP layer, RS256 for JWT verification

components.name: catch2
components.via: hkp-rt/tests — test framework, never linked into a shipped binary

components.name: eigen
components.notes: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft and header-only here; no obligation beyond notice.

components.name: espeak_ng
components.via: transitive: sherpa-onnx (via piper-phonemize) and the inflect TTS backend
components.notes: The only copyleft dependency linked into a shipped binary. This project is AGPL-3.0, and GPLv3 code may be combined with AGPLv3 code (AGPLv3 §13), so the combination is sound — but it does mean the desktop build cannot be relicensed to anything non-(A)GPL while espeak-ng is linked. Not built for iOS/Android (speech and inflect are both OFF there). The bundled ucd-tools is under the Unicode licence (COPYING.UCD) and parts are Apache-2.0 (COPYING.APACHE); all four texts are copied.

components.name: inja
components.via: 3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt — template rendering in the http-server service

components.name: json
components.notes: sherpa-onnx's own nlohmann/json checkout; the same project as nlohmann_json.

components.name: jthread
components.notes: Creative Commons Attribution on source code; attribution in the notices satisfies it.

components.name: jwt-cpp
components.via: 3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt — JWT verification in the runtime auth layer

components.name: llama_cpp
components.notes: Bundles vendored third-party licences of its own under licenses/; copied here.

components.name: minimp4
components.via: 3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt — MP4 demuxing for the mp4-to-wav service

components.name: nlohmann_json
components.via: 3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt (or sherpa-onnx's copy when speech is enabled)

components.name: onnxruntime
components.via: transitive: sherpa-onnx / inflect — a prebuilt binary release, never built from source
components.notes: Consumed as a prebuilt binary from one of two places: sherpa-onnx pulls a repackaged static build from csukuangfj/onnxruntime-libs, and the inflect backend pulls Microsoft's own release when sherpa is off (the Version column links whichever the scanned build used). Neither archive carries a LICENSE file, so the text stored under licenses/cmake/onnxruntime/ comes from the upstream repository.

components.name: piper_phonemize
components.notes: Vendors uni-algo (see its licenses/ directory), copied here.

components.name: saucer
components.via: CMakeLists.txt — the webview shell the desktop app is built on

components.name: crow
components.notes: Copied in without its LICENSE file; the upstream BSD-3-Clause text is stored under licenses/vendored/crow/. Two files inside carry their own terms: crow/TinySHA1.hpp (ISC-style, © Saurav Mohapatra) and crow/http_parser_merged.h (derived from Node.js http-parser, MIT). Both texts are stored alongside.

components.name: inflect
components.notes: ACTION REQUIRED: this is a first-party C++17 port of the Inflect v2 pipeline and currently carries no LICENSE file of its own. Two things need settling before a release: (1) add the project's own licence header/file to 3rdparty/inflect, and (2) record the upstream Inflect v2 licence, which governs the port as a derivative of its algorithm and, separately, the ONNX model weights the service loads at runtime. The weights are downloaded, not shipped, so they are a distribution question only if that changes.

components.name: mdns
components.notes: Released into the public domain by its author; the header states the dedication.

components.name: vcpkg
components.via: 3rdparty/vcpkg/ — the package manager itself (a git submodule, not shipped code)

components.name: yas
components.via: 3rdparty/yas/ — the YAS binary wire format used across runtimes
components.notes: Licence text is embedded in every header; the canonical BSL-1.0 text is stored here.
